title: Count Factors of Each Number
statement:
You are given an array of `n` positive integers. For each number, count how many positive integers divide it exactly (its **factors**, including `1` and the number itself).

Print the count for every number, in the same order as the input. For example, `12` has the factors `1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12`, so its count is `6`, and `1` has just one factor, itself.

The numbers can be large, so checking every value up to the number itself is too slow.
inputFormat:
The first line contains an integer `n`.
The second line contains `n` integers `a[0] ... a[n-1]`.
outputFormat: Print `n` space-separated integers: the number of factors of each `a[i]`.

examples.explanation: 100 has 9 factors (1, 2, 4, 5, 10, 20, 25, 50, 100). 97 is prime. 49 = 7 * 7 has the factors 1, 7, 49; the square root 7 must be counted only once.

hints: Factors come in pairs: if `d` divides `x`, so does `x / d`. One of the two is at most the square root of `x`.
Loop `d` from 1 while `d * d <= x`. Each divisor found adds 2 to the count (for `d` and `x / d`).
When `d * d == x` the two members of the pair are the same number, so add only 1.
